final.title: Check the process before you automate it
final.body:
Before you build a regression suite around a workflow, first check whether the workflow itself is stable enough to deserve one. For an owner-operator, that means picking one repeatable task — customer questions, invoices, or data work — and asking a simple question: does it produce the same kind of output most times, or do people quietly handle exceptions differently every week?

If the manual process is already inconsistent, automation will not fix that. It will just repeat the inconsistency faster. The better test is more basic: can you describe the process clearly enough that someone else would follow the same steps and reach the same result?

A practical next step is to document one workflow on a single page: trigger, inputs, steps, edge cases, and the point where a human still checks the work. That gives you a real basis for deciding whether to keep it manual, standardise it first, or automate part of it later. Bareni’s diagnostic starts with that same kind of workflow check, but the owner still makes the decision.
